nodes.title: Application runtime and dependency graph
nodes.description: Explains how Android launches Commons, initializes application-wide services and Dagger injection, and routes users into the main activity's signed-in or logged-out navigation.
nodes.body:
# Application runtime and dependency graph

## Android entrypoints

The manifest names `CommonsApplication` as the application class. `LoginActivity` is the launcher entrypoint; `UploadActivity` is also exported for image and audio `ACTION_SEND` / `ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE` intents, while `MainActivity` hosts the primary in-app navigation. The manifest also registers the account authenticator service, upload progress UI, and other feature activities and providers.

`CommonsApplication.onCreate()` initializes ACRA, obtains the singleton application component through `ApplicationlessInjection`, injects itself, and then configures logging, image loading, notifications, language lookup, and RxJava's global error handler. The application owns shared session, database-helper, preference-store, cookie, image-fetcher, and contribution dependencies.

## Dagger graph and Android component injection

`CommonsApplicationComponent` is the singleton Dagger component. It composes the application and networking modules with Android activity, fragment, service, content-provider, upload, contribution, search, depiction, and category modules. `ApplicationlessInjection` builds and caches that component for the process and exposes Android injectors. Activities are registered through `ActivityBuilderModule`; adding an injectable activity requires a corresponding binding there.

## Main navigation and login mode

`LoginActivity` handles authentication before entering the main screen. On `MainActivity` creation, the persisted `login_skipped` preference selects a logged-out pager that opens Explore; otherwise the signed-in navigation is set up, the previous Nearby tab may be restored, and stuck uploads are checked for resumption. Signed-in navigation loads fragments for Contributions, Nearby, Explore, and Bookmarks, while the logged-out pager uses a restricted `NavTabLoggedOut` set. The “More” action opens a different bottom sheet depending on login mode.

`BaseActivity` provides shared theme selection, font-scale adjustment, edge-to-edge setup, and cleanup of activity-scoped Rx disposables. Some activities, including LoginActivity, have their own delegate/lifecycle setup; check the concrete activity before assuming every screen follows the same base class.

## Where to look next

- [Networking and local storage](networking-and-storage.md) describes the separately wired API clients and database ownership.
- [Account and authentication flow](../workflows/account-and-authentication.md) follows login results into persisted account state.
- [Discovery and contribution browsing](../workflows/discovery-and-contributions.md) covers the main navigation destinations.
- [Media upload lifecycle](../workflows/media-upload.md) traces shared upload entrypoints through background execution.

## Source-grounded claims

Claims below describe runtime behavior verified against current source. They do not treat tests as a specification.

nodes.title: Networking and local storage
nodes.description: Describes the distinct HTTP client paths for MediaWiki services, JSON APIs, and images, plus Room, legacy SQLite migration, cookies, and preference-backed state.
nodes.body:
# Networking and local storage

## HTTP client paths

`NetworkingModule` provides a DI-managed OkHttp client with 120-second connection, read, and write timeouts, a shared User-Agent interceptor, logging, and an HTTP cache. `OkHttpJsonApiClient` and `CustomOkHttpNetworkFetcher` consume this injected client for JSON API calls and image retrieval.

Retrofit MediaWiki and Wikidata interfaces use a separate path: the module creates `CommonsServiceFactory` from `OkHttpConnectionFactory.getClient(cookieJar)`. That client attaches `CommonsCookieJar`, adds the common User-Agent header, logs basic request details with authorization and cookie headers redacted, and turns unsuccessful HTTP or MediaWiki error responses into failures. `CommonsServiceFactory` caches Retrofit instances by base URL. When changing transport behavior, check both client paths rather than assuming a single shared OkHttp configuration.

The `prod` and `beta` product flavors define their own Commons API, Commons web, image, campaign, and Wikidata endpoint values in `app/build.gradle.kts`. Retrofit service providers use those `BuildConfig` URLs to create endpoint-specific services.

Cookies are stored through `CommonsCookieStorage` in the default preference store. On load, the serialized value is decrypted; legacy plaintext or successfully decrypted content is saved again through the encrypted storage path. Logout clears the cookie jar.

## Local state and migrations

`AppDatabase` is the Room database (`commons_room.db`), currently schema version 22. Its entities and DAOs cover queued/completed contributions, depictions, upload status, reviews, nearby places, bookmarks, categories, and recent search/language data. `CommonsApplicationModule` registers the known Room migrations and also enables destructive fallback for migration paths without a registered migration.

The app also retains `DBOpenHelper` for the older `commons.db` schema. The Room 21-to-22 migration creates the corresponding Room tables and copies existing categories, bookmarks, bookmark items, recent searches, and recent languages from the legacy database when it exists. Check both the Room schema and legacy helper when modifying older tables or migration behavior.

Preferences are provided as a shared `JsonKvStore` over the app's preference store. The app uses that store for simple settings and serialized values; account credentials are managed separately through Android's `AccountManager` by `SessionManager`.

Contribution records persist upload state through `ContributionDao`: saves and updates refresh `dateModified`, and initial saves set `dateUploadStarted`. The upload workflow depends on these durable rows to resume work after the activity closes; see [Media upload lifecycle](../workflows/media-upload.md).

## Tests and extension points

`MigrationTest` exercises migration from a legacy database into Room and asserts representative data is retained. It is useful evidence for the migration path, but verify the current migration and schema directly when changing persistence. Focused upload and discovery behavior is covered in the linked workflow pages.

Network providers and database registration live in the Dagger modules. Add service interfaces through `CommonsServiceFactory` and `NetworkingModule`; add Room entities/DAOs to `AppDatabase` and register every migration in the shared application module.

## Source-grounded claims

Claims below describe the current source, not an assumption that all app requests share one client.

# Repository quickstart

This repository builds the Wikimedia Commons Android app. The Gradle settings currently include one application module, `:app`; the Android manifest names `CommonsApplication` and declares `LoginActivity` as the launcher. `UploadActivity` also accepts external image and audio share intents.

## Find the right guide

| If you are changing... | Start here |
|---|---|
| Application startup, Dagger injection, or activity navigation | [Application runtime and dependency graph](architecture/app-runtime.md) |
| MediaWiki/Wikidata API calls, HTTP clients, Room, or migrations | [Networking and local storage](architecture/networking-and-storage.md) |
| Login, account state, challenge codes, or CSRF tokens | [Account and authentication flow](workflows/account-and-authentication.md) |
| Selecting, describing, queuing, or uploading media | [Media upload lifecycle](workflows/media-upload.md) |
| Explore lists, contribution history, categories, or Nearby places | [Discovery and contribution browsing](workflows/discovery-and-contributions.md) |
| Gradle variants, CI, or deciding which tests to trust | [Build and test workflow](testing/build-and-quality.md) |

Use the manifest for Android component entrypoints, the Dagger component and builder modules for injectable Android components, and the feature flow page for the state owner and data source behind a screen. When tests disagree with production code, verify the current source path: several repository tests are ignored or stale, and the CI workflow does not currently run its instrumented-test step.

## Source-grounded claims

The app's purpose and runtime entrypoints below are grounded in the repository README and Android configuration.

nodes.description: Documents the app's Gradle variants, the unit-test and APK-build tasks used by CI, how instrumented tests are configured, and the limits of existing test evidence.
nodes.body:
# Build and test workflow

## Project and variants

This is a single Android application module, `:app`, built with Gradle and Kotlin. `app/build.gradle.kts` defines `prod` and `beta` product flavors and debug/release build types. Unit tests are Kotlin under `app/src/test/kotlin`; Android instrumented tests are under `app/src/androidTest/java` and use `AndroidJUnitRunner`. Unit tests include Android resources and can use Robolectric for Android APIs.

The Android CI workflow sets up JDK 17. On pull requests it populates `local.properties` with test account values from repository secrets and runs:

```sh
./gradlew -Pcoverage testBetaDebugUnitTestCoverage --stacktrace
```

It also builds both debug APK variants:

```sh
bash ./gradlew assembleBetaDebug --stacktrace
bash ./gradlew assembleProdDebug --stacktrace
```

The workflow contains a `connectedBetaDebugAndroidTest` emulator step, but that step is commented out. Instrumented tests therefore exist in the source tree but are not run by the checked-in Android CI workflow at present. To run them locally with a connected emulator or device, use:

```sh
./gradlew connectedBetaDebugAndroidTest
```

## Treat test results as evidence, not the specification

Test maintenance is uneven. Several upload presenter tests are annotated `@Ignore`, and some upload instrumentation tests are also explicitly disabled. Existing tests may encode assumptions from an older implementation or exercise only narrow behavior. Resolve discrepancies by tracing the current production path first, then use an active, focused test as supporting evidence; do not infer intended behavior from an ignored test.

Examples of narrower test surfaces include `MigrationTest`, which checks representative data after legacy-to-Room migration, and `LoginActivityTest`, which checks forgot-password navigation, signup navigation, and a generic orientation change. The login UI test does not assert credential retention, login-button enablement, or server-side authentication. The repository has additional tests for upload, browsing, preferences, and API clients, but their existence alone does not establish that CI executes them or that they cover the current behavior.

## Where to start

- For schema changes, read [Networking and local storage](../architecture/networking-and-storage.md) and run the focused migration test in the beta unit-test task.
- For login, upload, or discovery changes, follow the current source path and the relevant [account flow](../workflows/account-and-authentication.md), [upload lifecycle](../workflows/media-upload.md), or [discovery flow](../workflows/discovery-and-contributions.md) before relying on nearby tests.

## Source-grounded claims

Claims below describe checked-in Gradle and workflow configuration. CI command references distinguish active steps from commented-out steps.

nodes.title: Account and authentication flow
nodes.description: Follows MediaWiki login-token exchange, two-factor and email challenges, account persistence, session flags, cookie-backed API state, and logged-out browsing.
nodes.body:
# Account and authentication flow

## Interactive sign-in

`LoginActivity` collects the username, password, and optional challenge code, then delegates the network exchange to `LoginClient`. The client first requests a MediaWiki login token and submits the credentials with that token. OAuth two-factor, email authentication, password-reset, server errors, and transport failures are reported through `LoginCallback`; after a successful login it requests user information and attaches the user ID and groups to the result.

On success, `LoginActivity` sets the persisted `isUserLoggedIn` flag, asks `SessionManager` to update the Android account, and starts `MainActivity`. The activity can also save and restore credential fields and challenge state across recreation. A user can choose to skip sign-in; that sets the separate `login_skipped` preference and enters the logged-out navigation path, which exposes Explore rather than the signed-in destinations.

## Account and session state

`SessionManager` resolves the current account from Android `AccountManager` using the flavor-specific `ACCOUNT_TYPE`. It reads and stores the password through `AccountManager`, while the Boolean `isUserLoggedIn` flag lives in the default `JsonKvStore`. These values are related but distinct: `LoginActivity.onResume()` returns to the main screen only when both an account exists and the logged-in flag is true.

The app also registers `WikiAccountAuthenticatorService` for Android's account-authenticator action. For the app's account type, its add-account result launches `LoginActivity` with the authenticator response; other account types receive a non-login result. The authenticator's token, credential-update, and confirmation methods currently return placeholder bundles, so do not assume they implement a general Android token broker.

## Cookies and CSRF tokens

MediaWiki and Wikidata Retrofit requests use the persisted cookie jar described in [Networking and local storage](../architecture/networking-and-storage.md). `CsrfTokenClient` obtains a CSRF token for writes. If the asynchronous token request fails or returns an anonymous token while the app believes a user is logged in, it can clear cookies, reauthenticate using the stored account credentials, and retry once. The blocking token path also retries login before giving up; callers should handle `InvalidLoginTokenException` rather than treating an empty token as success.

The cookie-clearing `LogoutClient` used by this retry path only clears cookie storage. It is not the same operation as removing the Android account or clearing all application data.

## Tests

`CsrfTokenClientTest` uses the project's mock web server fixture for token and failure responses. Robolectric tests cover parts of `SessionManager` and the Android authenticator. These tests are useful pointers, but check the production callbacks and state owners directly when behavior has changed; see [Build and test workflow](../testing/build-and-quality.md) for known test-maintenance limits.

## Source-grounded claims

The claims below distinguish account storage, preference state, cookie refresh, and logged-out navigation.

nodes.title: Discovery and contribution browsing
nodes.description: Explains primary navigation, paged Commons browsing, server-backed user contribution history, and Nearby Wikidata discovery with a local place cache.
nodes.body:
# Discovery and contribution browsing

## Primary navigation

`MainActivity` owns the bottom-level app destinations. Signed-in navigation includes Contributions, Nearby, Explore, and Bookmarks; the logged-out route uses a restricted tab set and starts in Explore. The selected Nearby destination is remembered so the signed-in app can reopen it on a later launch.

Explore is itself a three-tab pager: Featured images, mobile uploads, and a map. The two list tabs wrap category-media fragments and request Commons media through `MediaClient`; the map tab can return to Nearby. Search and paging use separate data sources, so follow the specific feature's caller before changing pagination.

## Contribution history: local cache plus server

The self profile's completed contribution list is backed by the local Room contribution table. `ContributionBoundaryCallback` fetches the signed-in user's media from Commons when the list is empty or reaches its end, converts each media item into a completed `Contribution`, and saves it to the repository. This means the UI observes local persisted records while a boundary callback refreshes or extends that cache from the server.

Other users' profiles take a different path: `ContributionsListPresenter` uses `ContributionsRemoteDataSource` directly and does not attach the persistence boundary callback. Do not treat every profile list as the same local dataset. Pending, paused, and failed uploads are separate persisted contribution states managed by the upload flow; see [Media upload lifecycle](media-upload.md).

## Explore and paged search

`PageableMediaDataSource` maps requested page sizes and offsets to `MediaClient.getMediaListFromSearch`. The shared paging layer emits initial/loading/complete/error states, exposes a retry action for the last request, and reports empty results. Category search has a corresponding source backed by `CategoryClient`; that client filters hidden categories from mapped results.

The general search and paging components are reused across categories and depictions. When changing a query or list behavior, verify both the feature-specific load function and the shared paging lifecycle rather than relying only on adapter tests.

## Nearby places

Nearby discovery is driven by `NearbyParentFragmentPresenter` and `NearbyController`. The presenter skips a map refresh when the feature is locked, there is no network, or a search location is unavailable; map-center, location, and custom-query changes select different update paths. The fragment performs place queries off the main thread and reports empty/error results to the UI.

`NearbyPlaces` obtains nearby results from Wikidata queries through `OkHttpJsonApiClient`, expanding its search radius until it has enough results or reaches its configured maximum. Results are ordered for map display and enriched using a local place repository and bookmark DAO. The local place cache can also supply markers when searching an already-viewed map area offline. Nearby place bookmarks and cached place details are distinct from the server query results.

## Tests and source verification

Useful focused test entrypoints include `ContributionBoundaryCallbackTest`, `PagingDataSourceTest`, and `NearbyPlacesTest`. These cover representative boundaries but are not a guarantee of full end-to-end behavior; see [Build and test workflow](../testing/build-and-quality.md) for ignored tests and CI's current instrumentation-test configuration.

## Source-grounded claims

The claims below distinguish server-fetched contributions, local persistence, and remote map/search data.

nodes.title: Media upload lifecycle
nodes.description: Traces selected media through the upload editor, durable queued contributions, WorkManager processing, resumable MediaWiki stash chunks, and completion or failure.
nodes.body:
# Media upload lifecycle

## Selection and editing

Media can enter from the app's camera/gallery/custom selector or through Android share intents. `ContributionController` converts files selected in-app into an internal intent for `UploadActivity`, including the selected `UploadableFile` list and optional nearby-place or captured-location context. The manifest also lets `UploadActivity` receive external image/audio `SEND` and `SEND_MULTIPLE` intents.

`UploadActivity` resolves those inputs, creates media-detail fragments for each selected file, and then adds shared depiction, category, and license steps. The per-file editor also handles metadata, location, and thumbnail changes. Removing the last file from the editor displays cancellation and finishes that activity; this is cancellation before an upload contribution has been queued.

## Queue creation

The submit action reaches `UploadPresenter`. Submission requires an authenticated session; otherwise the presenter asks the user to log in. For an authenticated user, the upload model builds `Contribution` records from the selected files and metadata, media is prepared, each record is marked `STATE_QUEUED`, and it is saved through `UploadRepository`/`ContributionDao`. Once the sequence completes, the activity enqueues upload work and navigates to upload progress.

The persisted contribution contains the local media reference, metadata, categories, depictions, location/place information, and upload state. `ContributionDao` owns the durable state and timestamps, so the background worker can continue after `UploadActivity` is gone. Limited-connection mode changes the submit message; actual WorkManager execution still requires a connected network.

## Background processing and remote upload

`WorkRequestHelper` creates unique one-time `UploadWorker` work with a connected-network constraint and linear backoff. The worker processes queued contributions sequentially, ordered by upload start time, and persists the transition to `STATE_IN_PROGRESS`. It updates progress and chunk metadata through the contribution DAO.

`UploadClient` transfers media to the MediaWiki upload stash in 512 KiB chunks. It stores the returned chunk index, offset, and stash key on the contribution, allowing the client to resume from a valid stash for up to six hours. A missing/deleted contribution is treated as cancelled; pause and transfer failures remain distinct outcomes.

After a stash succeeds, the worker chooses a unique filename, submits the completed file with a CSRF token and generated page contents, and makes Wikidata edits when the contribution carries a place or depiction information. It then fetches the uploaded media record and replaces the queued record with a completed contribution. Media-upload failures are surfaced through notifications and persisted failure state. Optional place edits are attempted separately; the worker catches those exceptions and can still mark the media contribution completed. An invalid login also triggers application-data cleanup and a return to login.

## Cancellation and tests

There are different cancellation points: removing media from the pre-submit editor is handled by `UploadPresenter`; a queued or running contribution is represented in the database and checked by the worker/client. Do not equate the editor's last-image cancellation with cancellation of an already-started remote upload.

`UploadClientTest` covers selected stash-call success/error behavior and upload request fields. `UploadPresenterTest` has some ignored cases, so verify test assumptions against the current presenter and worker source; see [Build and test workflow](../testing/build-and-quality.md) for broader test limitations.

## Source-grounded claims

Claims below follow the current queue and worker implementation; nearby test cases are supporting evidence only.
